items.definition: A huge group of tiny water drops, or ice crystals, floating together high in the air.
items.example: That cloud is grey because it holds so much water.

items.definition: Any water that falls out of a cloud: rain, snow, sleet or hail.
items.example: The forecast said precipitation, so I took my umbrella.

items.definition: A ball of hot gas that makes its own light. The Sun is a star.
items.example: That bright dot is a star, shining all by itself.

items.definition: A big ball that goes around a star. It has no light of its own.
items.example: Mars is a planet, so it shines with borrowed sunlight.

items.definition: A ball of rock that goes around a planet and shows us the light it bounces back.
items.example: The Moon goes around the Earth once a month.

items.definition: The path one space object follows as it goes around and around another one.
items.example: The Moon is in orbit around the Earth.

items.definition: When one space object hides another. In a solar eclipse, the Moon hides the Sun.
items.example: We wore eclipse glasses to watch the eclipse safely.

items.definition: The hard outer coat of a tooth. It is the hardest part of your body.
items.example: The enamel is the shiny white part you can see.

items.definition: The softer layer under the enamel. It makes up most of the tooth.
items.example: The dentin is yellow, and a deep cavity can reach it.

items.definition: A soft, sticky film of germs and food that gathers on your teeth.
items.example: There was a lot of plaque near the gum.

items.definition: A hole in a tooth. It forms when acid from plaque weakens the enamel.
items.example: The dentist filled my cavity yesterday.

items.definition: The soft flesh that holds your teeth in place and protects them.
items.example: My gums bleed a little when I brush too hard.

items.definition: A mineral found in toothpaste. It makes the enamel stronger against acid.
items.example: This toothpaste has fluoride in it, so it protects my teeth.

items.definition: The sweet golden food that bees make from flowers.
items.example: The bees made twelve pots of golden honey.

items.definition: The home of a bear. It is a cave with a door, and it is warm inside.
items.example: Bo's den had a wooden door.

items.definition: The sad feeling you get when someone else has something you want. It is a feeling, not a plan.
items.example: Bo was jealous of Foxy's warm coat.

items.definition: A person you like and who likes you back. Friends like to spend time together.
items.example: Minh is my best friend.

items.definition: The long arm of a tree. Birds sit on branches and sing from them.
items.example: Sky landed on the branch beside her.

items.definition: To move your wings quickly but not very far. A fluttering bird stays in the same place.
items.example: Wren fluttered on the branch until her wings ached.

items.definition: To travel through the air without flapping your wings. The wind holds you up.
items.example: She slid over the wall. She was gliding.

items.definition: Not able to find the way home. If you are lost, you are not in trouble. You just need help.
items.example: Pip was lost, but he was not frightened of the dark.

items.definition: A smell that hangs in the air. Dogs can smell scents and follow them a long way.
items.example: Pip knew the scent of his own garden.

items.definition: The home a rabbit digs under the ground. It is soft and safe and it has a round door.
items.example: Pip's burrow has a round door and soft walls.

items.definition: A very small insect that makes its own light. It glows in the dark.
items.example: A firefly lit the path for Pip.

items.definition: A light you can carry in your hand. It goes wherever you go.
items.example: Grandmother Owl gave Pip a tiny lantern.

items.definition: Not feeling no fear, but going on anyway. Brave is about what you do, not what you feel.
items.example: Pip was brave and took one more step.

items.definition: A dark shape that appears when something blocks the light.
items.example: The old tree made a long shadow on the path.

items.definition: What really happened, even when it is not the easy thing to say.
items.example: An told his mother the truth about the blue bowl.

items.definition: Saying something you know is not true, on purpose, to make things easier for yourself.
items.example: He could have said the wind broke the bowl, but that would be a lie.

items.definition: Something you say you will do. People remember a broken promise for a long time.
items.example: An promised to tell his mother everything from then on.

items.definition: The yearly price of borrowing on the card, with most fees included. It is the number to compare two cards by.
items.example: This card has a 24 % APR, which is about 0.066 % a day.

items.definition: The most the bank will let you borrow on the card at one time. Going over it is usually refused and sometimes charged.
items.example: My credit limit is 2000 $, and I use about 600 $ of it.

items.definition: The period between two statements. Everything bought in one cycle appears on the next statement.
items.example: The billing cycle closes on the 12th, so my groceries appear on the 12th statement.

items.definition: The days between the statement date and the due date, during which you can pay in full without interest.
items.example: If I pay the statement balance inside the grace period, I pay no interest.

items.definition: The smallest monthly sum the card will accept. Paying only this keeps the balance, and the interest, alive.
items.example: The minimum payment is 25 $, so the rest of the balance stays on the card.

items.definition: The charge the bank makes for a late payment, on top of any penalty rate and any loss of your good history.
items.example: The late payment cost me a 35 $ overdue fee and my standard rate went up.

items.definition: The percentage change in the general level of prices over a period of time, usually a year.
items.example: The annual inflation rate was 4 %, so prices rose 4 % on average.

items.definition: The standard index of the price of a basket of goods and services bought by households. Its change over time is the headline inflation rate.
items.example: The consumer price index is the number the news report quotes.

items.definition: The year the price index starts from, set to 100. Changing it resets the index without changing any actual prices.
items.example: With last year as the base year, the index now stands at 104.

items.definition: Income measured in the money actually received, with no adjustment for changes in prices.
items.example: My nominal income rose, but not as fast as prices.
